title: Normative transcriptomic clues to thalamic developmental vulnerability in C9orf72-FTLD
authors: So, I.; Bouzigues, A.; Ferry-Bolder, E.; Cullen, E.; Russell, L.; Foster, P.; Farley, S.; Convery, R.; van Swieten, J. C.; Jiskoot, L. C.; Seelaar, H.; Galimberti, D.; Vandenberghe, R.; Laforce, R.; Bruffaerts, R.; Bertoux, M.; Lebouvier, T.; Solje, E.; Levin, J.; di Fede, G.; Thompson, A.; Le Ber, I.; Lara Migliaccio, R.; Kortvelyessy, P.; Schroeter, M. L.; Logroscino, G.; Otto, M.; Uzelac, Z.; Illan-Gala, I.; Kruger, J.; Nacmias, B.; Gerhard, A.; Langheinrich, T.; Ducharme, S.; Santana, I.; Tartaglia, C.; Masellis, M.; de Mendonca, A.; Rowe, J.; Graff, C.; Moreno, F.; Synofzik, M.; Borroni,
abstract: C9orf72 encodes a protein that is important for both typical neurodevelopment and homeostatic processes across the lifespan. Pathogenic C9orf72 repeat expansions constitute the most common genetic cause of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD). Collectively, preclinical models and clinical neuroimaging studies have observed smaller thalamic volumes in C9orf72-associated FTLD, including in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 repeat expansion carriers across 18 to 30 years old, supportive of potential neurodevelopmental origins. However, it is unknown whether asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers demonstrate volume differences in specific thalamic nuclei, as reported in older asymptomatic carriers and symptomatic patients; if so, normative transcriptomic patterns could reveal relevant neurodevelopmental and/or FTLD-related neurodegenerative processes. This study investigated volumetric MRI differences of the thalamic nuclei in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers, and examined spatial associations with normative thalamic transcriptomics from 8 weeks post-conception through middle age. Young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers (n=72) and non-carriers (n=48) were enrolled in the Frontotemporal Dementia Prevention Initiative across Europe, Canada, and the USA (ages: 18-30 years; sex: 57% female). Spatial associations between young adult thalamic nuclei volumes and normative transcriptomics from the Allen Human Brain Atlas were examined using complementary data-driven and hypothesis-driven approaches. Spatial expression patterns of transcripts of interest were characterized across prenatal and postnatal neurodevelopment using BrainSpan data. Smaller volumes of the pulvinar, mediodorsal, and lateral nuclei were observed in young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers. These nuclei showed higher normative expression of transcripts involved concurrently in neurodevelopmental and C9orf72-associated FTLD neurodegenerative processes (including lysosomal, autophagic, and small GTPase functions), and lower normative expression of CALB1, a marker of prenatal human thalamic development. Normative expression of CALB2 (another human thalamic development marker) yielded positive correlations with C9orf72 across prenatal development to adulthood. These findings identify candidate transcripts that may provide insight into the molecular architecture leading to smaller thalamic nuclei volumes in C9orf72-associated FTLD.

infographic.key_insight: Young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers already show smaller volumes in specific thalamic nuclei, and those nuclei map to transcriptomic programs linked to both prenatal thalamic development and FTLD-related biology.
infographic.clinical_relevance: This suggests thalamic vulnerability in C9orf72-FTLD may begin before symptoms, which could help refine early biomarker research and target disease mechanisms earlier in life.
method: Compared MRI thalamic nuclei volumes in asymptomatic C9orf72 expansion carriers (n=72) vs non-carriers (n=48), ages 18–30.
Linked nucleus-level volume differences to normative thalamic transcriptomics from the Allen Human Brain Atlas.
Used BrainSpan data to examine when key genes are expressed across prenatal and postnatal development.
infographic.evidence_signal: The study reports smaller pulvinar, mediodorsal, and lateral nucleus volumes in carriers, with spatial transcriptomic patterns implicating neurodevelopmental and lysosomal/autophagic/small GTPase pathways.
infographic.watch_item: Findings are associative and based on normative transcriptomic maps rather than direct tissue-level validation in the same individuals, so causal interpretation should be cautious.
infographic.paper_title: Normative transcriptomic clues to thalamic developmental vulnerability in C9orf72-FTLD

title: Stage-Aware and Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting IVF Implantation
authors: Sharma, H.; Yemelong, K.; Carmona, A.; Naghibi Harat, Z.; Rahmani, B.
abstract: Predicting implantation outcomes in vitro fertilization (IVF) is challenging because clinically relevant information becomes available at different points during treatment. In this study, we developed a stage-aware, leakage-conscious, and explainable machine-learning framework to predict implantation using a public IVF dataset. {beta}-HCG was excluded to avoid potential downstream target leakage. The data were divided into training, validation, and independent test sets. Several machine-learning models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest (RF), Extra Trees, XGBoost, and Hist Gradient Boosting, were optimized using stratified cross-validation. A fixed RF model was then evaluated at three stages of the IVF process, using baseline couple characteristics, gamete and fertilization variables, and embryological variables, respectively. Model performance improved as additional treatment-related information became available, with the largest improvement observed after the inclusion of embryological variables. The final RF model showed good predictive performance on the independent test set. The number of embryos was consistently identified as the most important predictor across RF, permutation, and SHAP analyses. Overall, the findings suggest that IVF implantation prediction becomes more accurate as later-stage treatment information is incorporated, particularly information related to embryological characteristics. The proposed approach also provides interpretable predictions while reducing the risk of information leakage. Further evaluation using independent clinical datasets is needed before the framework can be considered for clinical use.

infographic.key_insight: An explainable, stage-aware machine-learning model predicted IVF implantation better as more treatment-stage information became available, with embryological variables giving the biggest boost.
infographic.clinical_relevance: This could help support more informed IVF counseling and decision-making by providing interpretable risk estimates without relying on leakage-prone data.
method: Excluded beta-HCG to reduce target leakage.
Trained and tuned Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Extra Trees, XGBoost, and Hist Gradient Boosting with stratified cross-validation.
Tested a fixed Random Forest model across three IVF stages and used permutation and SHAP for explanation.
infographic.evidence_signal: The model was trained on a public IVF dataset, split into training, validation, and independent test sets, and showed good performance on the independent test set.
infographic.watch_item: The framework still needs validation on independent clinical datasets before it can be considered ready for real-world use.
infographic.paper_title: Stage-Aware and Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting IVF Implantation

title: MedMatch: a standardized medication order format for data science and natural language processing applications
authors: Blotske, K.; Henry, K.; Zhao, X.; Li, T.; Tilley, A.; Cargile, M.; Murray, B.; Gao, Y.; Smith, S. E.; Barreto, E.; Bauer, S.; Sohn, S.; Liu, T.; Bennett, T. D.; Sikora, A.
abstract: BackgroundWithout automation, evaluation of medication management with large language models (LLMs) is largely limited to resource-intensive clinician evaluation. The purpose of this study was to develop a standardized medication structure (MedMatch) that supports automated evaluation. MethodsOur goal was to create a medication order format with face validity to a clinician panel that maximizes clarity and safety. We used a multi-step process including (1) clinician survey of medication orders, (2) clinician survey of order appropriateness, (3) order sentence structure formation, (4) benchmark experiment development, and (5) GPT-5-chat testing across multiple experiments, which included assessment of ability to transform a medication order into MedMatch format and identify the route of an order sentence and ability to identify missing order components. ResultsFirst, lexical overlap analysis demonstrated pattern norms with specific components appearing most commonly in order of drug name, dose, unit, route, and frequency. Secondly, formal written orders consistently showed low omissions and high overlap and were deemed more appropriate as computer-generated orders. Third, MedMatch formats were created for oral and intravenous routes. Fourth, benchmark datasets and an abbreviation document were created. Fifth, GPT-5-Chat accuracy on MedMatch order standardization was highest in intravenous push (96.7%), oral liquid (86.1%), and intravenous intermittent (85%) categories. Overall performance was 77.6%. Identification of missing order components was improved with the MedMatch format (76.8% vs. 66.7%). ConclusionsThis is the first attempt to create and assess standardized medication order formatting to support benchmarking performance of LLMs. Limitations identified here demonstrate the need for medication-specific methodology.

infographic.key_insight: The study introduces MedMatch, a standardized medication order format designed to make medication-order evaluation easier and more consistent for LLMs and NLP systems.
infographic.clinical_relevance: A shared order structure could improve automated assessment of medication documentation quality and help reduce the need for time-intensive clinician review.
method: Surveyed clinicians on real medication orders and order appropriateness
Created standardized order sentences for oral and IV routes, plus benchmark datasets and an abbreviation guide
Tested GPT-5-chat on formatting, route identification, and missing-component detection
infographic.evidence_signal: GPT-5-Chat achieved 77.6% overall accuracy, with highest performance in IV push (96.7%) and improved missing-component detection using MedMatch (76.8% vs. 66.7%).
infographic.watch_item: The format is still early-stage and may not generalize across all medication types, workflows, or institutions without further validation.
infographic.paper_title: MedMatch: a standardized medication order format for data science and natural language processing applications

title: Language eligibility criteria and enrolled racial and ethnic composition in US clinical trials: a cross-sectional study
authors: Tolas, A.; Du, L. Y.; Schutz, N.; Schmiedmayer, P.; O'Sullivan, J. W.; Johnson, A.; Longenecker, C. K.; Sarraju, A.; Rodriguez, F.; Yang, E.; Kim, D. S.
abstract: BACKGROUNDFederal policy now requires sponsors to submit diversity action plans for clinical trials, yet the modifiable features of trial design associated with enrolled composition remain poorly characterized. English-language proficiency requirements are written into eligibility criteria and recorded as free text in a public registry, making them visible and, in principle, amenable to revision, but their relationship to enrolled composition has been examined only within single disease areas and in small samples of trials. We examined whether these requirements and documented language accommodation were associated with the racial and ethnic composition of enrolled participants. METHODS AND FINDINGSWe conducted a cross-sectional study of interventional trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov with at least one US site and posted results, using a registry snapshot retrieved in October 2026. The primary cohort comprised the 44,487 trials with exclusively US sites, of which 21,924 (49.3%) reported baseline race and 17,434 (39.2%) reported baseline ethnicity with counts that reconciled with the posted denominator. Both exposures were classified from free-text eligibility criteria using regular expressions validated against independent physician review of 150 trials. For the English-language requirement classifier, sensitivity was 88.2% and specificity was 99.2%. The outcome was the trial-level proportion of enrolled participants in each category, analyzed using generalized linear models adjusted for intervention class, therapeutic area, sponsor, phase, enrollment, sites, start year, US Census region, and the population composition of the trials site states. An English-language proficiency requirement appeared in 5,736 trials (12.9%); its prevalence rose from 7.4% of trials starting in 2010 to 26.2% in 2023 (odds ratio [OR] per decade 2.91, P<0.001), whereas documented accommodation, an eligibility statement allowing participation in a language other than English (Spanish in 99.9% of flagged trials), remained rare (788 trials, 1.8%). The requirement was associated with lower enrolled proportions of Asian (OR=0.85, 95% CI 0.77-0.93, P=0.001) and Hispanic/Latinx participants (OR=0.85, 95% CI 0.79-0.91, P<0.001), with no evidence of an association for White participants (OR=0.99, 95% CI 0.95-1.04, P=0.75). Documented accommodation was associated with a higher proportion of Hispanic/Latinx participants (OR=3.23, 95% CI 2.82-3.71, P<0.001). Geographic adjustment did not change the statistical significance of the requirement associations and attenuated the accommodation association. The main limitations were the cross-sectional design, which precludes causal inference; the restriction of enrollment analyses to trials reporting baseline demographics, which were more recent than those without such reporting; and possible misclassification of automatically classified exposures. CONCLUSIONSEnglish-language proficiency requirements became more than three times as common between 2010 and 2023 and were associated with lower enrolled proportions of Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants. Less common documented language accommodation was associated with a higher enrolled proportion of Hispanic/Latinx participants. Because these criteria are investigator-written and publicly recorded, they may be a tractable target for improving enrollment equity, although whether revising them changes who enrolls requires prospective evaluation.

infographic.key_insight: US clinical trials that required English proficiency enrolled fewer Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants, while language accommodations were uncommon.
infographic.clinical_relevance: Making eligibility language requirements more flexible may be a practical lever to improve trial diversity and reduce avoidable participation barriers.
method: Cross-sectional analysis of 44,487 interventional US trials on ClinicalTrials.gov with posted results.
Eligibility criteria were mined from free text using validated regular expressions for English-language requirements and language accommodations.
Enrolled racial/ethnic composition was modeled with adjusted generalized linear models accounting for trial and sponsor factors.
infographic.evidence_signal: The English-language requirement classifier performed well against physician review (88.2% sensitivity, 99.2% specificity), and the requirement was linked to lower enrolled proportions of Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants.
infographic.watch_item: Because this is observational registry research, the association may reflect unmeasured trial or site factors, and many trials still lacked complete race/ethnicity reporting.
infographic.paper_title: Language eligibility criteria and enrolled racial and ethnic composition in US clinical trials: a cross-sectional study

title: Personalised normative cardiac phenotyping reveals clinically relevant heterogeneity in cardiac shape and outcome risk
authors: Li, Z.; Bai, W.; Matthews, P. M.; Kainz, B.; Qiao, M.
abstract: Standard cardiac biomarkers such as ejection fraction, ventricular volumes, and strain compress complex three-dimensional heart dynamics into a small set of predefined measurements, leaving clinically important heterogeneity unrecognised. Here we propose a personalised normative cardiac frame-work in which each individual is compared to a digital twin representing expected healthy cardiac function given their age, sex, and body habitus. We show that structured patterns of deviation from these normative twins, discovered through systematic exploration of a generative cardiac dynamics space, constitute novel dynamic phenotypes that are not captured by conventional biomarkers. Applied independently to two UK Biobank cardiac cohorts with distinct shape representation, a 128-dimensional four-chamber statistical shape descriptor (HeartSSM, n = 52,365) and a 64-dimensional deep generative latent space from a conditional variational mesh autoencoder (MeshHeart cVAE, n = up to 39,376), we identify reproducible, continuous deviation-from-normative-twin scores (three discrete deviation phenotypes in the HeartSSM cohort) that improve cardiovascular risk stratification beyond ejection fraction, ventricular volumes, myocardial mass, and strain. The strongest effect was seen for incident atrial fibrillation among individuals with preserved ejection fraction ([≥]50%): incremental C-index {Delta}C = +0.068 (5-fold cross-validated {Delta}C = +0.063; likelihood-ratio P = 3.3 x 10-8), with a separate, smaller effect for incident stroke in the same preserved-EF subgroup in the independent MeshHeart cVAE representation (which showed no signal for atrial fibrillation) ({Delta}C = +0.024, P = 2.6 x 10-4). Both effects were checked against placebo controls in which the deviation scores were replaced by Gaussian noise. To test whether the normative twin generalises beyond UK Biobanks specific scanning and processing pipeline, we applied the MeshHeart cVAE normative twin, unmodified, to an independent external cohort of healthy volunteers imaged at a different hospital (Gen-Scan/Hammersmith, n = 315): deviation scores in this cohort were of comparable magnitude to the UK Biobank healthy reference (ratio of means = 1.09; Mann-Whitney P = 1.4 x 10-5), indicating that the normative twin captures cross-site-transferable structure rather than a scanner- or pipeline-specific artefact. Our findings suggest that cardiac phenotyping can move beyond predefined measurements toward data-driven dynamic phenotypes that better capture the heterogeneity underlying cardiovascular disease risk, even among individuals whose ejection fraction appears normal.

infographic.key_insight: A personalised “digital twin” baseline can reveal hidden cardiac shape-and-function patterns that conventional measures like ejection fraction may miss.
infographic.clinical_relevance: These deviation phenotypes improved prediction of future cardiovascular events, especially atrial fibrillation in people with preserved ejection fraction, suggesting a path toward more precise risk stratification.
method: Built normative cardiac twins using age, sex, and body habitus to define expected healthy heart shape/function.
Compared individuals against two independent shape representations: HeartSSM (statistical shape model) and MeshHeart cVAE (deep latent mesh model).
Derived deviation scores and tested whether they added prognostic value beyond standard biomarkers, with placebo-noise controls and external validation.
infographic.evidence_signal: In UK Biobank cohorts, deviation scores improved risk prediction beyond standard biomarkers, with the strongest signal for incident atrial fibrillation in preserved-EF participants (ΔC up to +0.068; likelihood-ratio P = 3.3×10^-8) and a smaller independent signal for stroke in the alternate representation.
infographic.watch_item: The approach relies on specific imaging pipelines and shape representations, so broader clinical deployment will need robust standardisation and validation across scanners and populations.
infographic.paper_title: Personalised normative cardiac phenotyping reveals clinically relevant heterogeneity in cardiac shape and outcome risk
